program_alignment.central_question: Can a physically declared noisy repeated D4 record support causal just-in-time decoding without hidden-state or future leakage?
program_alignment.scientific_layer: WP4 physical observation and fault-tolerance prerequisite
upstream_dependencies: released deterministic E2 two-stage causal interface

program_alignment.information_value: A schedule pilot is uninterpretable unless data faults, hidden D4 state, public repeated reports, applied corrections, and private logical truth form one normalized causal transition law. This audit can falsify that prerequisite without Monte Carlo cost.

question_and_knowledge_states.question: Do the current primary-source rules and verified project interfaces jointly specify every factor of a normalized action-conditioned repeated D4 transition kernel and its private logical scorer?
question_and_knowledge_states.smallest_claim: The audit can identify which kernel factors are source-supported, project-defined, or missing; it cannot establish noisy D4 performance.
established_external_knowledge: Jing 2025 Supplemental Appendix D gives a localized time-like-herald example, likelihood ordering, and a 3D-decoder proposal, not a complete multisite repeated D4 channel.
Jing 2026 Section VII introduces spatial physical-error, temporal measurement-error, and fusion-channel variables and explicitly leaves numerical implementation and benchmarking for future work.
Lyons and Brown define a local noisy D(S3)/D(Z3) circuit and causal JIT schedule, but this does not supply a D4 transition kernel.
current_project_evidence: Lab 004 supplies a normalized static D4 observation sampler conditional on one spatial physical error and a truth-side logical score.
Lab 005 G supplies a generic binary-data/binary-syndrome/categorical-report schema but no D4 state evolution.
Lab 005 E1 supplies source-bounded local projector state updates and classical reports but not a complete stochastic spatial trajectory.
Lab 005 E2 verifies action-bound two-stage causal composition only when the physical post-action report is externally supplied.
assumptions_and_constraints: anyon-free ground-state-relative logical criterion from resolved thread-008
public schedules may see only causal reported records and action digests
truth, physical faults, fusion-state internals, future rows, and logical labels remain private
no independent-per-round fusion resampling may be assumed unless a state-update argument supports it
competing_outcomes: The existing static sampler, E1 instrument, E2 action binding, and private homology scorer compose into a complete normalized Markov kernel.
Classical readout and scoring are complete, but cross-round hidden D4 state evolution or action-conditioned post-flux generation is missing.
Only a circuit- or density-state-level model can close the kernel; a phenomenological schedule pilot remains scientifically underdetermined.
question_and_knowledge_states.resolution_rule: Evaluate every kernel factor separately. A complete factor must have an operational input/output law, normalization or deterministic identity, causal ownership, and a source or explicit project-extension label. One passing factor cannot mask another missing factor.

primary_source_search.effect: licenses the localized projector/time-like-herald audit but not a general memoryless repeated channel
defines spacetime fusion/error variables and measured-syndrome dependence; records that numerical implementation remains future work

research_basis.remaining_gap: No existing artifact proves that the static D4 sampler and local repeated-projector instrument define one joint cross-round action-conditioned probability law.

scientific_model.candidate_state: private round-indexed D4 physical/error state X_t on the paper L=2 periodic lattice, including the residual physical chain and only the hidden projector information required for the next transition
scientific_model.candidate_transition: P(X_{t+1}, O_{t+1} | X_t, F_t, A_t), where F_t is a declared data/readout fault increment, A_t is the applied public correction, and O_{t+1} is the causal public report
scientific_model.public_observation: round-indexed typed syndrome/fusion reports, schedule-visible detector history, and exact action/report digests
scientific_model.private_sidecar: fault increments, residual physical chain, hidden projector outcomes/state digest, seed or exact branch weight, and ground-state-relative logical class
required_invariants: each probabilistic factor is normalized on exact tiny support
readout-only faults change reports but not hidden physical state
data-only faults change physical state before projective readout
corrections update the residual physical state before the bound post-action measurement
causal serialization contains no truth or future rows
private logical scoring occurs only after a frozen completed transition
scientific_model.resolution_limit: Static inspection and exact tiny enumeration can establish completeness or localize a missing factor; they cannot validate hardware correlations or estimate any performance quantity.

registered_methods.design: source/interface ledger plus exact paper-L=2 limiting-case checks for every available kernel factor
registered_methods.inputs: frozen primary PDFs and the released Lab 004/Lab 005 modules and evidence listed above
registered_methods.verification: perfect, one-data-fault, one-readout-fault, one-action, winding, and replay cases only
registered_methods.analysis: classify each K1-K4 factor as complete, project-assumption, localized-only, or missing and report the earliest missing dependency
registered_methods.budget: under five CPU minutes and 1 GiB; deterministic inspection/exact enumeration only; zero Monte Carlo samples
registered_methods.stop: do not implement a stochastic generator, choose a memoryless/stateful approximation, or run a schedule comparison if any required factor is missing
registered_methods.escalation: consult the researcher only if the audit leaves multiple materially different physical transition laws that cannot be discriminated by the sources or bounded exact checks
